claims.text: An ultrathin, conformal Ni interlayer is deposited on tungsten particles before composite assembly and sintering.
The Ni interlayer enhances copper wetting on tungsten.
The Ni interlayer promotes interdiffusion at the W–Cu interface.
Improved wetting and interdiffusion produce a uniform, void-free W–Cu contact.
The modified W–Cu interface improves thermal transport and mechanical durability under irradiation.
W particles or interconnected W regions embedded in a Cu matrix are typically produced using vapor-coated W powders followed by sintering.
The composite is to be sintered at 800–1000 °C.
A sintering temperature of 800–1000 °C is well below tungsten's melting point.
The intended service boundary includes high heat flux and fusion-reactor irradiation.
The Ni layer lowers the interfacial energy mismatch between W and Cu.
Ni-mediated interdiffusion and copper spreading suppress interfacial void formation.
Ni-mediated interdiffusion and copper spreading suppress phase separation.
Improved interfacial bonding increases thermal conductivity.
Improved interfacial bonding increases mechanical resilience under irradiation.
Relative to the vapor-coated powder baseline, the Ni-interlayer composite will have significantly fewer interfacial voids and enhanced interfacial bonding.
Relative to the vapor-coated powder baseline, the Ni-interlayer composite will have improved thermal conductivity and preserved mechanical integrity.
Vapor-coated W powders sintered by conventional spark-plasma sintering achieve near-perfect initial W–Cu contact.
The stated vapor-coated W-powder spark-plasma-sintering baseline retains residual porosity.
The stated vapor-coated W-powder spark-plasma-sintering baseline exhibits phase separation.
The magnitude of thermal and mechanical improvement depends on Ni-coating uniformity and sintering conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a void-free W–Cu contact, whereas the predicted outcome only commits to significantly fewer voids; the absolute and relative formulations are not equivalent.
